sources.title: Learning from sanctioned government suppliers: a machine learning and network science approach to detecting fraud and corruption in Mexico
sources.inspection: Selected extracted passages from Abstract, Introduction, Datasets, Feature engineering, train/test design and validation; fetch capped at 55,000 characters
sources.finding: Uses buyer–supplier graphs and positive–unlabelled learning; flags the absence of confirmed negative labels, selected sanctions, company/contract mapping and temporal versus transductive evaluations.
sources.localDecision: Use grouped, time-respecting validation and disclose unknown labels. Do not label every Indian contract of a sanctioned supplier corrupt, infer hidden control from centrality, or transfer model scores across countries.
limits: Study concerns Mexican procurement, not this project.
The paper assigns all contracts of sanctioned companies positive labels under a strong assumption; that rule is not adopted here.
SCAR selection of labelled positives is admitted rarely valid.
Reported minimum precision and relative gains are not Indian model calibration.

sources.title: TempASD: Temporal Anomalous Subgraph Discovery in Large-Scale Dynamic Financial Networks
sources.dateBasis: KDD conference begins 3 August; paper publication day not independently fixed
sources.inspection: Selected extracted Abstract, algorithm motivation and sections 5.1–5.2; fetch capped at 55,000 characters
sources.finding: Temporal subgraph anomaly discovery evaluated on Ethereum/NFT transaction datasets, with labelled PlusToken data and pseudo-label/reference-method limitations for others.
sources.localDecision: Keep transaction-time order and original units when bank/payment data ever exists. Do not run Benford anomaly scoring over mixed budgets, awards, grants and alleged transfers.
limits: Blockchain transfer networks differ fundamentally from this documentary relation graph.
Higher abnormal degree is not proof of laundering.
Code link observed in paper; repository not installed or independently benchmarked.

sources.inspection: Selected extracted release, identifiers, implementation transactions and amendment sections; fetch capped at 55,000 characters
sources.finding: Transactions represent actual flow using payer/payee; award/contract values and versioned amendments remain distinct.
sources.localDecision: Retain tender/award/contract/transaction identifiers and version history; no summation across stages.
limits: Our CONTRACT is a local evidence schema, not an assertion of OCDS conformance.

sources.title: Models in Microeconomic Theory, Expanded Second Edition — chapter 16, Extensive games
sources.dateBasis: Chapter version date printed in inspected text
sources.inspection: Selected extracted introduction, section 16.1, definitions 16.1–16.6 and perfect-information limitation; author page separately checked; fetch capped at 18,000 characters
sources.finding: A game specifies players, feasible histories, authority to move, preferences and strategies. Perfect information is an explicit assumption.
sources.localDecision: Use actor/authority/constraints/known-information/feasible-options worksheets, preserving unknown private preferences. No numeric utility or equilibrium is estimated from outcome alone.
limits: The institutional records do not provide complete actions, preferences or information sets.
No claim to have read the whole book.
Author/publisher lawful public access; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; no claim to relicense the book.
